issues.display_title: Issue #488: Refresh Location Grouping After Post Location Edits
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refresh Location Grouping After Post Location Edits

Summary

Location grouping is now re-triggered after EditPostDescription, and the previous group fields are cleared before the worker processes the post. This prevents an edited post from retaining or matching its own stale location group.

Changes

Commit c5f8b354

  • Added PostFunctions.SendWorkerLocationGrouping(postId) after a successful EditPostDescription update flow.
  • Moved the existing AddPostCompleteEmbed grouping dispatch into the completed post-processing branch, after its Redis, Elasticsearch, and Maps Panorra work.
  • Preserved the LocationGrouping queue and { "post_id": ... } payload.

Commit f6549780

  • Added these values to the EditPostDescription update map:
"location_group":      nil,
"location_group_slug": nil,
  • The fields are cleared in the same database update as location_name and location_post.
  • The worker subsequently resolves and stores the new group name and slug.

Data Flow

  1. EditPostDescription parses the submitted or selected location.
  2. The API updates location_name and location_post while clearing both grouping columns.
  3. After the database update succeeds, the API publishes post_id to the LocationGrouping queue.
  4. The worker reads the latest location data from posts.
  5. ResolveLocationGroup no longer sees the edited row as an existing non-null group candidate.
  6. The worker writes the resolved location_group and location_group_slug back to the post.

Compatibility

  • No endpoint, request parameter, HTTP status, or response field changed.
  • No RabbitMQ queue or payload field changed.
  • No grouping algorithm changed.
  • Existing post group values are intentionally unavailable between the API update and worker completion.
  • Because EditPostDescription always dispatches grouping, description-only edits also clear and recompute the group.

Verification

Review of both commits confirms:

  • Worker dispatch occurs after the post update in EditPostDescription.
  • Both group fields are reset in the update map.
  • AddPostCompleteEmbed dispatch remains after successful completion processing.
  • The existing API response block is unchanged.
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • These commits did not add a dedicated database or worker regression test, so the asynchronous regrouping result still requires the runtime check below.

Recommended runtime check:

  1. Edit a post from PT. GoThru Media Indonesia to Yogya Grand Kepatihan Bandung.
  2. Confirm both grouping fields become NULL after the API update.
  3. Confirm the LocationGrouping worker consumes the post ID.
  4. Confirm both fields are repopulated for the new location.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostDescription.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostCompleteEmbed.go

Git

  • Worker trigger: c5f8b354.
  • Group reset: f6549780.
  • The existing API collection environment edit is unrelated and remains untouched.
  • These documents are local because docs/ is ignored by Git.

Problem

EditPostDescription updates location_name and location_post, then sends the post to the LocationGrouping worker. When the post already has location_group and location_group_slug, those old values can survive the edit.

The grouping resolver prioritizes an existing post with the same place_id and a non-null location group. Because the edited post already contains the new location_post but still contains its old group, it can match itself and return the stale group instead of resolving the new location.

Example:

  • Previous location: PT. GoThru Media Indonesia.
  • New location: Yogya Grand Kepatihan Bandung.
  • location_name and location_post change successfully.
  • location_group and location_group_slug remain associated with the previous location.

Scope

  • Dispatch the LocationGrouping worker after EditPostDescription successfully updates the post.
  • Reset location_group and location_group_slug to NULL in the same post update.
  • Let the existing worker recompute both fields from the current location data.
  • Keep the AddPostCompleteEmbed grouping dispatch in its completed post-processing path.
  • Preserve the existing API response and asynchronous worker payload.

Behavior Boundary

  • EditPostDescription continues to update description, location, category, visibility, and timestamp as before.
  • The response status and JSON structure remain unchanged.
  • The worker message still contains only post_id.
  • Existing grouping rules, sanitization, proximity thresholds, and slug generation remain unchanged.
  • Group fields may temporarily be NULL until the worker finishes.

Out of Scope

  • Changing ResolveLocationGroup matching rules.
  • Changing LocationGrouping queue names or message schemas.
  • Synchronous grouping inside the API request.
  • Updating existing posts through a database migration or backfill.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Editing a post clears its existing location_group and location_group_slug.
  • The API dispatches the post ID to the LocationGrouping worker after the update succeeds.
  • The worker can assign grouping values based on the updated location.
  • New completed embed posts continue to dispatch grouping after successful post processing.
  • API response compatibility is preserved.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-09-03 in commits c5f8b354 and f6549780.
